concept.body: Power of a point: every line through P meets the circle in two points whose distances from P multiply to the SAME number. Inside (crossing chords): piece × piece = piece × piece. Outside (secants): external × whole = external × whole. Tangent limit: PT² = external × whole. The engine is AA similarity from same-arc inscribed angles.

widget.prompt: Chords cross at P: pieces 3 and 8 on one, 4 and x on the other. x = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 24 is the shared product — x is its factor partner: 24/4 = 6.

steps.body: From angles to lengths. Two chords crossing at P inside a circle obey **PA · PB = PC · PD**: the products of the two pieces match. Why: joining the endpoints creates two triangles with equal inscribed angles (same arcs) — similar by AA, from the similarity course — and the proportion cross-multiplies into the product rule.

widget.prompt: Two chords cross inside a circle. One is split into pieces 4 and 6; the other into 3 and x. Find x.

commonErrors.feedback: 7 = 4 + 6 − 3 plays an addition game — the rule MULTIPLIES pieces: 4·6 = 3x ⇒ x = 8.
4.5 = 3·6/4 shuffles into a proportion of the wrong pairs — products of SAME-chord pieces match: 24/3 = 8.
24 = 4 · 6 is the power itself (the matched product) — x is its partner piece: 24/3 = 8.

steps.body: Outside the circle the same law holds in costume: for two secants from P, **PA · PB = PC · PD**, where both distances are measured FROM P — so each product is the secant's **external part times its whole length**. Same AA-similarity engine, same matched products.

explanationVariants: First secant: 5 × 12 = 60. Second: 4 × (4 + x) = 60 ⇒ 4 + x = 15 ⇒ x = 11.

widget.prompt: From external point P, one secant has external part 5 and whole length 12. A second secant has external part 4; its chord (the part inside the circle) has length x. Find x.

commonErrors.feedback: 15 = 60/4 is the second secant's WHOLE length — the chord is what's left after the external 4: 15 − 4 = 11.
8.75 = 5·7/4 multiplied external × internal — the rule pairs external × WHOLE: 5·12 = 4·(4 + x) ⇒ 11.
60 is the power of the point (each matched product) — x solves 4(4 + x) = 60: x = 11.

steps.body: Let one secant rotate until its two intersection points merge: it becomes a **tangent**, and near × far collapses to **PT · PT = PT²**. The tangent-secant law: **PT² = PA · PB** (external × whole). One law, three costumes — chords, secants, tangent — all called the *power of the point* P.

widget.prompt: From P, a secant has external part 4 and whole length 9. Find the tangent segment PT from the same point.

commonErrors.feedback: 36 is PT SQUARED — take the root: 6.
20 = 4 × 5 multiplied external × internal-chord — the law pairs external × WHOLE: 4 × 9 = 36, PT = 6.
4.47 = √20 roots the wrong product — use external × whole: √36 = 6.

widget.prompt: The crossing-chords proof joins chord endpoints to form two triangles. Why are they similar?

options.label: Two pairs of inscribed angles stand on the same arcs (plus vertical angles at P) — AA similarity
options.feedback: Same-arc inscribed angles are congruent (ch1's corollary); AA fires, and the side proportion cross-multiplies into PA·PB = PC·PD.

options.label: They're congruent by SSS
options.feedback: The triangles are usually different SIZES — it's similarity (AA), and the proportion becomes the product rule.

options.label: Both contain the center
options.feedback: The center may lie in neither — the engine is same-arc inscribed angles giving AA.

options.label: They're both right triangles
options.feedback: Right angles aren't guaranteed anywhere in the figure — the matched INSCRIBED angles (same arcs) supply the AA.

widget.prompt: P sits inside a circle. One chord through P splits into 2 and 9. EVERY chord through P splits into pieces whose product is ?

commonErrors.feedback: 11 = 2 + 9 adds — the invariant is the PRODUCT: 2 × 9 = 18, the same for every chord through P.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 2 × 9 = 18 — the power of P: one number, every chord.

hints: The sight line grazing the rim is a TANGENT; the walk straight to the far side is a SECANT through the center.
PT² = external × whole = d × (d + 14), with PT = 12 and diameter 14.
144 = d² + 14d — rearrange to d² + 14d − 144 = 0 and use the quadratic formula.
explanationVariants: d² + 14d − 144 = 0 doesn't factor over the integers — the quadratic formula gives d = (−14 + √(196 + 576))/2 = (−14 + √772)/2 ≈ 6.89 m (the negative root is unphysical).
d = (−14 + √772)/2 ≈ 6.89 m by the quadratic formula.

widget.prompt: You stand distance d from the NEAR rim of a circular well of diameter 14 m. Your tangent sight line to the rim measures 12 m. Find d (2 decimals).

commonErrors.feedback: 12 m is the TANGENT length — d solves d(d + 14) = 144, giving ≈ 6.89 m.
10.29 = 144/14 divides the power by the diameter — the secant's whole length is d + 14, not 14: d(d + 14) = 144 ⇒ ≈ 6.89.
2 solves d(d + 14) = 32-ish — the power is 12² = 144: d ≈ 6.89.

takeaways: Inside: crossing chords, PA·PB = PC·PD — AA similarity via same-arc inscribed angles.
Outside: secants pair external × WHOLE; the tangent limit gives PT² = external × whole.
The matched product is the POWER of the point — one number for every line through P.
